topic: Moser's Circle Problem: The Deceptive Power of Patterns
target_audience: High school students with an interest in discrete mathematics and pattern recognition.

sections.title: The Hook: How many slices can you get?
lecture_lines: Place dots on a circle's edge.
Connect every pair with a chord.
animations: Create a single vertical cut through the circle using a knife [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/knife.svg] (#FFFFFF).
Create a second horizontal cut forming four pieces [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/knife.svg] (#FFFFFF).

sections.title: Pattern Recognition (The Trap)
lecture_lines: It seems like powers of two.
animations: Display sequence of cuts (1, 2, 3) and pieces (2, 4, 7) using [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/pizza.svg].
Highlight the difference between geometric sequence and actual result using [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/cake.svg].
Show the jump between expected pattern and reality (#FF4500).

sections.title: The Counter-Intuitive Reality
animations: Show a third cut creating 7 total pieces using a [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/knife.svg] (#FFFFFF).
Visualize each new cut adding more pieces than before.
Use arrows (#00CED1) to show the area added by each cut.

sections.title: The Combinatorial Formula
lecture_lines: Combinations define the number of regions.
Use the sum of binomial coefficients.
animations: Decompose the formula into its core components step by step.
Animate the mapping of n cuts to the total area using a [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/knife.svg] (#FFD700).
